column1: # Drink the potion colours whose results the shipped game prints, to measure
# the lines `inventory.md` section 7 describes but does not quote.
# This is a lottery on the result line. `inventory.md` section 7 (Potions): "a
# variation roll gives one chance in sixteen to force the Orange sleep effect
# and one chance in sixteen to replace the effect with a random potion row",
# and section 7.2 adds that "Results belong to the effective colour after the
# existing variation roll". So about one drink in eight prints a line for a
# colour other than the one in the bottle, and the two sides never share a
# seed. A run whose result lines disagree has measured that roll rather than
# the engine and must be re-run; the structure around them - the `Item:` and
# `On who:` rows and their spacing - is what this scenario pins.
# Seeded rather than walked to. The walk-up form of this scenario scripted its
# way in from the town gate, and the resident walks its own schedule while
# those steps run, so the two sides arrived with it in different cells and
# every later beat compared unrelated windows (`cleak/u5-engine#22`).
# `qa/tools/reseed.py` replayed that walk once into the seed named below.

column4: Journey Onward on the seeded cell
